handoff: Changes requested, 2 blocking: glab's own write verbs (mr/issue note, update, mr approve/revoke) are allowed so AC3 holds only for gh; AC7's limitations entry is pinned by no test. Tests and typecheck green; 6 minor/nit notes.

findings.title: glab comments, edits and approvals on merge requests and issues are allowed
findings.detail:
AC3 / user story 25 refuse 'creating, editing, commenting on, reviewing, readying, merging, closing or reopening pull requests, merge requests and issues'. REVIEW_WRITES holds only gh's verb names, and glab's names differ for the same writes: `glab mr note` / `glab issue note` (comment), `glab mr update` / `glab issue update` (edit), `glab mr approve` / `glab mr revoke` (review). Probe through shellRefusal: `glab mr note 1 -m x`, `glab issue note 3`, `glab mr update 1 --title x`, `glab issue update 1`, `glab mr approve 1` all return null (allowed). `glab mr --help` lists note/update/approve/revoke as the merge-request write commands. The core tests cover glab only for mr create/merge, issue reopen, labels, releases and api.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Give forgeRule a per-tool write set: for glab add note, update, approve and revoke (on mr and issue where they exist); add those glab cases to the 'refused with the remote rule's reason' table in packages/core/test/unit/hook-refusals.test.ts.

findings.title: The limitations entry (AC7, verifier: test) is pinned by no test
findings.detail:
AC7: 'the limitations entry says the hooks are a reminder, not a sandbox, and names what they miss (shell writes under run state, unlisted remote writes, other norn commands) as still forbidden by the brief; the docs lint passes' — verifier: test. The entry's wording is right, but `grep -rl 'not a sandbox' packages test scripts` finds no test; only the docs lint (glossary/links) runs over it, which would stay green if the entry were dropped or reworded.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Add a unit-tier test (e.g. next to the existing docs tests under test/) that reads docs/limitations.md and asserts by terms: 'reminder, not a sandbox', run state, remote writes not on its list, and the norn commands other than brief/done/ask/stuck.

findings.title: `git checkout -- -b` is refused although a path after `--` should be allowed
findings.detail:
CHECKOUT_SWITCH_FLAGS is matched against every argument, including those after `--`; shellRefusal('git checkout -- -b') returns no-switch. AC2: 'a git checkout <path> ... after --, is allowed'. Rare file name; errs toward refusing.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Only look for switch flags before a `--`.

findings.title: A rev-parse timeout drops the hook fact from the trace
findings.detail:
resolvedCommits throws on timeout inside gatedAnswer, which runs before appendHookTrace (line 166); the catch answers allow (as D12 wants) but the PreToolUse fact is never traced.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Catch in resolvedCommits and return [] (allow), so the trace line is still written.

findings.title: Global options with a separate value defeat the subcommand lookup
findings.detail:
afterOptions knows only -C/-c (git) and -R/--repo before the group (gh/glab): `git --git-dir x push` and `gh pr --repo o/r merge 3` are allowed. D6 names only -C/-c, and the tokenizer is meant to err toward allow, so a note rather than rework.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Optionally add --git-dir/--work-tree/--namespace and skip -R/--repo after the group too.

findings.title: checkoutNames repeats gitRule's checkout parsing (Duplicated Code)
findings.detail:
checkoutNames re-runs afterOptions(GIT_VALUE_OPTIONS), CHECKOUT_SWITCH_FLAGS and bareCheckoutName from gitRule (lines 89-98); if they drift the cli resolves names core never checks.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Share one helper that returns the checkout's switch flag or bare name.

findings.title: The cap test relies on the push test running before it
findings.detail:
'tool refusals leave the end-of-turn cap its full number of blocks' proves the cap is untouched only because the previous test traced five refusals into the same run; run alone it proves less.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Refuse a push inside this test before counting.

findings.title: Three asserts call checkoutNames directly
findings.detail:
The Plan says the tokenizer is covered through hookAnswer on whole commands. checkoutNames is the exported core-to-cli fact contract, so asserting it is defensible, and the neighbouring hookAnswer asserts prove the same behaviour.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Keep or drop; no rework needed.
